result:
I audited the submission against the assignment, the notebook framework, the workers' raw logs, and my own re-runs. Round 1 appended to `validator/checklist.md`.

## What I verified (and how)

**Coverage** — re-converted the `.doc` myself and read all three channels; `strings` on the raw file finds exactly Q1 (20) + Q2 (20) + Q3 (30) = 70 pts. All three answered, in order, cover page included as the handout demands. The "Page 1 of 3" footer is a Word field, not missing content. No question depends on a figure.

**The code is real and is what was run** — `shared/gt_framework.py` reproduces the notebook's framework cells line-for-line, so the harness wasn't tampered with. All 207 printed listing lines appear verbatim in the sources that produced the logs. I ran cells 14, 18, 19 and 22 end to end in my own directory: all four work.

**Numbers recomputed, not trusted** — I re-ran the full 30-epoch cell 14 from scratch and got **val 0.5160 / test 0.5496 / epoch 30**, exactly the bolded Table 1 row. My own cell-22 run landed inside Table 4's printed spread. Every pair count in Tables 2 and 3 reproduces exactly (73/120/189/200/266; 63,236/78,485/804,349/108,965/139,417), as do all five `params` figures, all Table 4 means and sds recomputed from the per-seed logs, and Table 2's 3-seed means and half-ranges. Side claims check out too: smallest ZINC molecule 9 nodes, LapPE channel RMS 0.0115, degree 2 on 50.6% of atoms, bond ids {1,2,3}, and `segment_attention` genuinely absent from PyG 2.8.1.

**R9** — both GraphGPS quotes are verbatim and I read past them in the paper. The "irreparably fail…" quote does target GraphTrans's 2-stage design, and the following sentences support rather than undercut the submission's reading. Eqs. (9)–(11) of Appendix D.1 say what the answer says they say.

**R8** — 354 / 383 / 506 prose words for 20/20/30-point implementation questions. Well inside budget; no padding.

I did not find a wrong answer, a missing sub-part, or a compile problem. What I did find:

## Defects

- **[D1.1] major** — `final/p2.tex:44–49`. `\lstdefinestyle{p2python}` omits `columns=fullflexible, keepspaces=true` and `breakindent`, so the Q3 listing on PDF p.8 renders as `class HybridGTLayer ( nn . Module ) :` / `self . norm_ffn`, and wrapped lines flush to column 0 (`summed."""`, `D/heads]`) — copy-paste out of the PDF yields broken Python. Q1/Q2 use `p1py` (`p1.tex:5–14`), which sets all three and renders cleanly, so the same document typesets its code two different ways across three pages. In an assignment whose deliverable is the implemented code, this is the one thing a marker sees at a glance. Fix: give `p2python` the same three options as `p1py`.
- **[D1.2] minor** — p1.tex, Q1 prose (PDF p.2): "moves it by 0.0119, inside the ±0.0100 seed half-range of Table 2". 0.0119 is outside ±0.0100. The conclusion survives against the 0.0200 seed *spread*; the sentence as written does not. Rephrase to the spread, or to "comparable to".
- **[D1.3] minor** — PDF p.2 vs p.9. Table 1 gives plain attention test 0.7013 and the demo 0.4957; Table 4 gives 0.693 and 0.495 for the same two baselines (its own seed-0 runs were 0.6908 and 0.4830 — `problems/p2/logs/baseline-{plain,demo}_s0_e30.log`). Both are honestly measured under different protocols and thread counts, but nothing in the document says so. One clause in Table 4's caption fixes it.
- **[D1.4] minor** — p1.tex, Q1 prose (PDF p.2): "the constant eigenvector $D^{1/2}\mathbf{1}$". For the symmetric normalised Laplacian that vector is constant only on a regular graph, and ZINC molecules are not. The formula is right; drop "constant".

VERDICT: FAIL
